articles.title: Crackle Network
articles.summary: Fine crack network cuts sharp channels through smooth shine; dried-clay crazing, low contrast, even coverage. Still reads: a large-scale cracked-plate pattern across panels, like old lacquer crazing or dried lake bed, with a mottled sheen.
articles.what: Creates crack and craze roughness network like dried clay — sharp channels cut through smooth surface Up close: A network of dark, smooth-edged cracks, 3-8 px wide, splitting the surface into irregular plates 40-120 px across, like dried mud or crazed glaze. Plates stay shiny while the channels read dull and dark; satin shows it softly, metallic shows it sharper where the band is bright. From a distance: Still reads: a large-scale cracked-plate pattern across panels, like old lacquer crazing or dried lake bed, with a mottled sheen. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Weather, Wear & Track (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: fine.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Weather, Wear & Track", or search for "Crackle Network".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof and sides: big panels show whole plates
Avoid small trim where the cracks get lost
Cracks run through numbers as dull lines; large bold numbers stay readable.
Visible cracks, soft contrast; a pleasant aged look
Pairs well with: matte, gloss, metallic.
pitfalls: Not a cracked paint pattern: it adds no colour, only dull lines in the shine
Not hammered metal: cracks are thin channels around flat plates
Avoid: reads as dirt at distance, low contrast may vanish on dark base.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.title: Add it as an overlay
examples.goal: Layer Crackle Network over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.

articles.title: Galvanic Corrosion

articles.what: Voronoi two-metal partition — roughness spikes and metallic drops at dissimilar metal contact seams Up close: Sparse small ragged clumps of speckle about 10-20 px, like pitting or white crusty corrosion blooms, scattered randomly on an otherwise smooth surface. articles.title: Sandblast Strip
articles.summary: Soft matte blotches of bare-metal roughness scattered over painted gloss; low-contrast, micro-fine grain. Reads as a frosted, sandy, slightly dull sheen; the grains blur into a soft matte-ish haze that breaks up the reflection.
articles.what: FBM blob-shaped sandblasted zones — bare metal roughness adjacent to unblasted painted surfaces Up close: Dense, random, very fine salt-and-pepper grain a few pixels per grain, like media-blasted metal or sandpaper. No pattern, direction or blobs visible in this crop. The grain makes the highlight sparkle with a gritty frosted look, subtle on satin and clearly gritty on metal. From a distance: Reads as a frosted, sandy, slightly dull sheen; the grains blur into a soft matte-ish haze that breaks up the reflection. No colour change. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Weather, Wear & Track (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). articles.title: Stress Fractures
articles.summary: Metal fatigue crack tree along gradients; near-zero metallic, max roughness, worn dull. Disappears at distance, leaving at most a faint streaky grain in lit areas.
articles.what: Metal fatigue crack tree grown along FBM gradients — crack pixels near-zero metallic, max roughness Up close: Hairline wavy cracks, one pixel wide, running slanted across the panel about 20-30 px apart, drawn as faint dotted bright lines in the highlight on metallic and dark thin lines in the floor reflection. On satin they are barely there. It looks like fine ripples or crazing, not a branching tree. From a distance: Disappears at distance, leaving at most a faint streaky grain in lit areas. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Weather, Wear & Track (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker).
